intro: I didn't start by knowing how to build everything. I started by being curious enough to try.

chapters.title: Pet's Health
chapters.subtitle: Where It All Began
chapters.role: Concept Development, UI Design, Basic Application Logic
chapters.summary: An idea for better pet care became my first exploration of interfaces, teamwork, and application logic.
chapters.challenge: Turning an ambitious pet-care idea into an early interactive prototype.
story: Pet's Health was one of my first experiences in software development. The project aimed to create a digital platform that made pet care easier by organizing medical records, veterinary appointments, pet communities, and pet-related services and products.
I contributed to developing the original concept, designing interfaces in Figma, and implementing basic functionality through Microsoft Power Apps.
Although the project remained an early prototype, it introduced me to the process of transforming an idea into a digital experience.
chapters.lesson: I learned that every application begins with understanding a problem, not just writing code.
chapters.transition: From designing interfaces to building websites with code.

chapters.title: CECAM
chapters.subtitle: Learning to Build
chapters.summary: A real school. A larger idea. My first steps into building the web with HTML and CSS.
chapters.challenge: Organizing a real institution’s information into an accessible website.
story: CECAM was one of my first attempts at building a larger website for a real educational institution, Centro Escolar Católico Alberto Masferrer.
I worked on developing an informational website using HTML and CSS, exploring responsive layouts, navigation systems, image galleries, and the organization of academic information.

Although the project was never completed and remained an early-stage prototype, it helped me develop a stronger understanding of web development and gave me confidence to approach more complex projects.
chapters.lesson: I discovered that building a website isn't just about making it look good, but about making information accessible and easy to navigate.
chapters.transition: From creating digital interfaces to exploring technology beyond the screen.

chapters.title: POT-C
chapters.subtitle: Beyond the Screen
chapters.summary: With Klani, our composting prototype, I stepped beyond interfaces and into electronics and physical making.
chapters.challenge: Bringing an environmental idea into both a digital experience and a physical prototype.
story: POT-C was an environmental technology project developed with my team at ¡Supérate! Fundación Poma.

The project introduced Klani, a smart compost bin prototype designed to transform organic household waste, such as fruit peels, vegetable scraps, and eggshells, into natural compost through a five-phase process.
My primary responsibility was developing the front end of its informational website using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Tailwind CSS.
The website included interactive environmental statistics, charts, image galleries, and a 3D visualization of Klani.
I also helped with the 3D printing of physical components and the assembly of the prototype's internal electronic circuitry.
The project was presented during Expo 2025, Roots of Legacy.
chapters.lesson: I realized that technology doesn't have to stay inside a screen. Programming, electronics, and creativity can work together to bring physical ideas to life.
chapters.transition: From combining hardware and software to developing more complex digital platforms.

chapters.title: Plant Bud
chapters.subtitle: Connecting Everything
chapters.role: Front-End Development, Back-End Development, AI Integration, Teamwork
chapters.summary: A collaborative platform where AI, plant care, and local services became parts of one experience.
chapters.challenge: Connecting many features and technologies into one coherent application.
story: Plant Bud became one of my most ambitious collaborative projects, developed alongside a team from ¡Supérate! Fundación Poma.
The platform was designed to make plant care easier through artificial intelligence and digital services.

Its main features included AI-powered plant health analysis through photographs, personalized care recommendations, plant information, AI-assisted garden redesign using uploaded images, professional gardener hiring, nearby nursery discovery, and a reward points system for payments made through the platform.
I contributed to both front-end and back-end development, helping integrate different technologies and functionalities into a larger application.
We also presented the project at Expo Tech.
chapters.lesson: I learned that building a complex application isn't just about developing individual features. It's about connecting everything into a meaningful and functional experience.
chapters.transition: From developing ambitious collaborative platforms to creating independent solutions inspired by personal experiences.

chapters.title: Beyond
chapters.subtitle: Creating with Purpose
chapters.role: Independent Development, Front-End and Back-End Logic, Educational Technology
chapters.summary: My own experience preparing for AVANZO became a free learning tool for other students.
chapters.challenge: Turning the challenge of studying several subjects into useful, independent practice.
story: Beyond was born during my final year of high school while preparing for the AVANZO 2026 exam in El Salvador.
After experiencing how challenging it could be to study multiple subjects at once, I decided to create a free educational platform that could help other students prepare more effectively.
The platform includes interactive practice across Mathematics, Language and Literature, Natural Sciences, and Social Studies.
Students can complete 20-question timed exams with a 60-minute limit, take extensive 100-question diagnostic assessments, receive feedback, and learn from detailed explanations of incorrect answers.
Beyond allowed me to apply my programming experience to a project I developed independently, combining educational content, interactive assessment systems, and user-centered design.
chapters.lesson: I learned that something I experienced personally could become the starting point for a tool capable of helping others.
chapters.transition: From building individual projects to bringing my entire journey together.

chapters.title: My Portfolio
chapters.subtitle: Building My Own Space
chapters.role: Independent Web Development, UI/UX, Interactive Experiences
chapters.summary: A personal space where my technical and creative sides finally meet.
chapters.challenge: Bringing different projects and experiences together without sacrificing usability or performance.
story: My personal portfolio represents the combination of everything I've learned throughout my previous projects.
Rather than creating a simple website to display my work, I wanted to build an interactive digital space that reflects both my technical and creative sides.

The portfolio includes separate desktop and mobile experiences, animated interfaces, interactive project galleries, detailed documentation, an integrated PDF viewer, a 3D model viewer, and a locally developed chatbot capable of answering questions about my projects and experience without relying on external AI services.
It also incorporates performance optimizations, accessibility features, and automated testing.
chapters.lesson: I discovered that everything I had learned could come together in one place, creating something that truly represents who I am and what I love building.
chapters.transition: The next chapter is still being written.

future.title: Still Learning. Still Creating.
future.description: Every project taught me something new. Every challenge pushed me further. And every idea reminds me that there's still so much left to discover.
future.closing: The next chapter hasn't been written yet.
